Asha Patel: PRD intake — we need an acceptance matrix + eval suite for launch readiness. Recent customer rollouts showed silent quality regressions after minor quant/patch changes. Problem statement: we don't have a concise set of pass/fail criteria and edge-case checks that engineering, QA, and PM can agree on. Goal is to capture measurable acceptance criteria, non-goals, and a minimal automated harness so we can gate alpha->beta->ga.
Marta Kim: quick q — do we want separate gates per customer tier (hosted vs dedicated vs private)?
Asha Patel: yes, split by deployment mode where metrics differ (latency/cost). core quality criteria should be shared.
Sam Ortiz: suggestion: create an `eval_core` prompt set (~500 prompts) + adversarial edgecases (~100) and run batch evals with semantic-similarity + human spot checks. Example metric: cosine similarity of embeddings + response intent match. Keep thresholds conservative.
Priya Desai: from QA perspective: need a runnable checklist for regression tests and explicit flag matrix for flaky prompts. Also need automation so releases run the harness in CI and fail the job on regressions.
Ben Cho: we should include a clear "falldown" behavior test: when a newer variant underperforms, the system must auto-fallback to the previous verified variant within our routing SLOs. test should simulate high load and latency to confirm fallback triggers and that user-visible replies remain coherent.
Leo Grant: success metrics we care about: user-facing quality (NPS/CSAT delta), unit economics (tokens/call), and operational SLOs (p95 latency). Need to quantify acceptable tradeoffs for cost vs quality.
deploy-bot: Ticket created: PROD-EVAL-1287 — acceptance-matrix draft
Asha Patel: draft acceptance criteria proposal (first pass):
```
Acceptance criteria (all must be satisfied for a rollout):
- Core eval pass rate >= 95% on `eval_core` (n=500) using semantic-similarity threshold >= 0.78 AND human spot-check pass >= 90%.
- Regression delta <= 1.5% on semantic-similarity vs pinned baseline.
- Latency targets:
  - Dedicated: p95 <= 120ms
  - Hosted: p95 <= 250ms
  - Private (on-prem): documented per-customer baseline
- Memory/kv-cache overhead increase <= 10% vs baseline.
- Fallback behavior validated: under simulated overload/latency, fallback to pinned variant occurs within 100ms and observable error rate does not increase > 0.5%.
- Security/safety checks: no new high-confidence toxic responses (toxicity score threshold) in `safety_suite` (n=200).
- CI gating: harness must run in pre-prod and mark builds failed on any hard violation.
```
Sam Ortiz: add quantitative acceptance for hallucination-sensitive tasks: e.g., factuality precision >= 92% on `facts_v1` set.
Priya Desai: add test: rollout dry-run against 5 production customer datasets (anonymized) to catch tenant-specific regressions.
Ben Cho: edge cases we should enumerate now:
- very long context with KV-cache boundary conditions
- mixed-language prompts (code + prose)
- partial input corruption (truncated JSON or broken tokens)
- prompt injection attempts and tool-calling safety
- very low-token responses (1-3 tokens) correctness
Asha Patel: non-goals (call these out explicitly):
- We will NOT use success metrics tied to downstream product KPIs (e.g., MRR) for alpha gating — those are longer-term.
- This PRD will not define post-GA customer migration plans.
Asha Patel: proposed success metrics (for the release window):
- Regression-free deploys for 6 consecutive canary runs
- No critical customer incidents linked to model quality for 30 days post-release
- Variants that increase cost by > 15% must show >= 2% absolute quality improvement to be considered
Marta Kim: request — please add ownership rows (PM/ENG/QA/SE) and expected due dates in the PRD. Also link to sample prompt sets.
Asha Patel: will draft the PRD with sections: problem, goals, non-goals, acceptance matrix, eval harness README, runbook for fallback, ownership + timeline. Target: initial PRD by tomorrow EOD. Can owners volunteer now?
Sam Ortiz: I'll own the eval harness + CI integration (ETA 2w)
Priya Desai: QA test cases + automation — I'll own (ETA 10 days)
Ben Cho: solutions eng will provide 5 anonymized customer datasets for dry-run (ETA 1 week)
Leo Grant: I'll validate success metrics and cost thresholds, help define per-tier SLOs
Asha Patel: thanks — I'll produce the PRD draft and ping for reviews. If anyone has strong objections to acceptance thresholds above, flag now. :thumbsup:
Marta Kim: looking good. :+1:
Priya Desai: ack
